newsitem.title: INDIA: India to inject 3 bln rupees into sick UCO bank.
newsitem.headline: India to inject 3 bln rupees into sick UCO bank.

text.p: India has agreed to pour three billion rupees ($84 million) into state-owned UCO Bank to pull the ailing bank out of the red, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said on Monday.
The news agency quoted bank chairman and managing director Sharda Singh as saying the funds would help UCO earn a target profit of one billion rupees in 1998/99 (April-March).
"UCO Bank has drawn up a three-year strategic revival plan which has been accepted by the Finance Ministry and the Reserve Bank of India," the bank said in a statement.
Of India's 27 state-owned banks, UCO Bank is one of the eight that are making losses. The bank lost 25.91 billion rupees in 1995/96.

The bank plans to close up to 25 loss-making branches, and is aiming for 20 percent growth in deposits, a 20 percent reduction in non-performing assets (NPA) and a 40 percent increase in non-interest income.
An overall improvement in customer service, including an increase of 30 minutes in business hours, is also part of the plan, the statement said.
PTI quoted Singh as saying NPA currently amounted to 13.96 percent of deposits and that the bank hoped to bring these down to five to six percent. ($1 = 35.7 rupees)
